notes.title: Release Date be Upon Ye! Dicealot Coming Out October 9th!

notes.title: Behind the Dice: Voice Overs!
notes.notes: [p]This week on Behind the Dice, we asked the devs: [i]What was the process of recording the voice overs for the characters like?[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Luckily I have a lot of gregarious friends! Although I am of the firm belief that anyone can do VO, everyone has a great natural voice that can be used for fantastic characters, its just a case of finding the right fit. For Dicealot, I gathered some of my close friends (and my better half), and we winged most of it. I always have some lines written for each character, but its usually about half the necessary VO, and then we ad-lib the other half. [/p][p][/p][p]Its generally a case of me laying out what I thought about for the characters personality, and then whoever wants to do a take for them, we just go with that. There's some back and forth and little directing by me, but its really an exercise in silliness for the most part. Its always one of my favourite days for game production, even if I then have to spend hours cutting around the off-mic laughter to get the good takes![/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]I couldn't get any photos of them in the process of recording the VO, and I am not an artist by any means. So instead, here is my stick figure rendition of friends having fun recording some voice overs! [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/6e5e2e791f5553b4db02b9c299c3e266bfaf9665.png"][/img][/p][p]....Just pretend you can see the fun through their expressionless faces. [/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Behind the Dice: Shops
notes.notes:
[p]This week, on Behind the Dice, we asked the devs: [i]Tell us about another feature / mechanic in the game![/i][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]Another feature we added quite late into the game's life, was the choice between shops. Originally the player would find the same shop inbetween each fight, there are lots of benefits to this such as predictability (from the player's POV) and simplicity, for us. This omni-shop worked well, but I found it a bit restricting in terms of what we're able to deliver in that 'between fights' space.[/p][p][/p][p]I decided to separate the shops, and offer the player a choice of randomly selected shops instead. This is admittedly more complicated, and less obvious to the player on its face, so we've already been through a couple of iterations to make sure the player understands what they're being faced with when there is a choice to be made. [/p][p][/p][p]Overall, I really like the moment of decision when faced with the shops, it gives the player more agency over their build and allows for some tough decision making, which is always good in a roguelike I would wager. It also gives us plenty of modular space to add more encounters that aren't straight shops, where there would have been no room for these encounters previously.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/8deef69f23b20d68d644c0e98d56a613846ef12e.png"][/img][/p][p]⠀⠀[/p][hr][/hr][h2][/h2][p][/p][p]Look at this, absolutely cracked[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/7246951a107ca4de6bf48580e87185ee2ae766a2.png"][/img][/p][p]Roll any dice and thou shalt be rewarded.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]Until next time!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/3e7dc9ea33f7d302d7b7d956bf5ddd6a6684c0d2.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Behind the Dice: Animations
notes.notes: [p]Wake up dice rollers, it's Behind the Dice time again![/p][p][/p][p]This week, we asked the devs: [i]Show off a feature you’ve added to the game - could be art, animation, gameplay feature! How does it work? Why did you add it?[/i] [/p][p][/p][p]We added a big screen-wide banner to declare the player has rolled a Farkle!, and also to declare the encountering of rare mobs. I wanted to add it initially, inspired by the ‘’Rare Catch!’’ banner that appears on Sega Bass Fishing, and then when making it realised it would be a vast improvement on the square title pop-up we were currently using to announce a Farkle.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/bc66f96d524c1cc2b27e2b5e3efcfc1481205f98.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Farkle Sprite Sheet[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/6362135153d1411e2bdffcaed436037058aadad9.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]Farkle Animation[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Before Dicealot, I had never done any animation, so getting used to creating sprite sheets was a whole process. (I have also developed a deep sympathy for full time animators... their poor hands.) As with most things, toward the end of the project everything becomes a little smoother as there is nothing you're doing/making for the first time (ideally). These banners were an opportunity to push the visual feedback on some more un-loved interactions, and make the game feel a little more alive. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/86dbc9b85d36001ad5c317afc2de7617261c9ca8.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Slash Sprite Sheet[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/82122d50f5bbe59d8dd86e082e4b29a326067ce4.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]Slash Animation[/i][/p][p][/p][p]It can be a bit of a challenge from a visual hierarchy point of view also, as one imagines that [i]all[/i] interactions would benefit from some jaunty animation (and they likely would), but we already have quite a lot going on on the screen, and so using moving elements to direct player's attention is a really useful tool, one that becomes less effective the more banal things that are animated.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]The little details are so cool and really make you appreciate artists that much more eh? Hope you enjoyed this week's Behind the Dice as much as I did - sprite sheets are so much fun (to look at)! Have a lovely weekend and see you in the next one![/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]P.S., Look at these numbers[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/7c30a98b7e654acc974c1534cdeecb7f1902f1de.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Credits: [url="https://discord.com/invite/W4VzWHDF2U"]Discord[/url] community member djsac[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/5ed4cd74f0da083f3669ef53008a268d3761bbfe.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Behind the Dice: Challenges
notes.notes: [p]It's that time of the week again, the one where we pester the devs with little questions, keeping them hostage and making them give us cool answers - all for you guys, the community![/p][p][/p][p](For legal purposes that is a joke, the devs are happy and well, willing to do these dev diaries.)[/p][p][/p][p]This week, we asked them: What have you been finding more challenging? For example, anything not going quite to plan, or needing unexpected workarounds?[/p][p][/p][p]Here's what they had to say:[/p][p][/p][p]It has been a design challenge to author good, unique feeling end-game content that doesn’t require overhauls of existing systems, or adding new mechanics, as we lack the time to do that with our schedule.[/p][p][/p][p]The solution to this issue has been to come up with new ways to use mechanics and systems we already have, in creative ways. Utilising stuff we have already implemented in ways it was not originally intended to be used, allows us to add more variety to the effects and gameplay, without requiring whole system overhauls.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]How do you like them apples?[/h3][p][/p][p]Try this one trick that doctors HATE.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks to [url="https://discord.com/invite/W4VzWHDF2U"]Discord[/url] community member djsac for this one! [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/c868dcc2d86dc54512204716ae01a312ec608cd7.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Also, if you were ever curious as to how professional I am when it comes to these posts[/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/e4097495d1f3e766d1f3a9a21060769353e37521.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]I'm so good at this.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]That's all for this week's Behind the Dice, and we hope to see you in next week's![/p]

notes.title: Behind the Dice: Iterations
notes.notes:
[p]This week on Behind The Dice, we're showing off a bit of concept art and how the UI has evolved![/p][p][/p][p]
                               [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/2860d4392a01902b81876085e74f6ff746a9028f.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Here's one of the characters from concept days to what it looks like now! The original sketch captured the vibes the devs were going for, but you can see how much more personality and detail emerged in the final iteration. Those colours alone are so cool![/p][p][/p][p]Check out what Dicealot [i][b]used[/b][/i] to look like - [/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdmDNkT8p7WYby9i-di8eN5iQMzDAY7422Xl4EbaEsu9Hdad8b9cT9bjbijg5rWT-u6e3sJJkHt9lHUkKK4G1TiiP7qu6duRI0RyivgtK5K3LHCf-SNK-KZ6c7GgEh8zFwLIfzzbA?key=QWlOo39JTJoTP-Zj4uU8oA"][/img][i]This is [b]at[/b] [b]least[/b] a year old now![/i][/p][p][/p][p]It's giving old, medieval tavern vibes. I have no idea why I'm so reminded of my Old School RuneScape days looking at this.[/p][p][/p][p]From the devs: [/p][p]Originally the game was supposed to be a much cosier, tavern themed roguelike. I wanted to do a full 3D tavern interior, angry mailed fist slamming against the table top when your opponent loses etc., but we basically didn't have the time to do any of that if we wanted to have a presentable prototype for publishers in any sort of timely fashion. So, the original UI was attempting to echo this initial vibe. However I don't think it landed, and we ended up with something that felt very ''generic medieval'' to me, which I was not a fan of.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXepL8kSeJlLb8OFpc4l2Rha5xvCLUQqr2Vxmr2kMQQU1HSDuwqGoelQMD-Wj-gY08J3-SJLkMOr0_KsXJ7JpNP8AQh39QS5I24OzYIpqMOUxSEm3I3kKxBx6Ja3kLPmLxPw3Tj50w?key=QWlOo39JTJoTP-Zj4uU8oA"][/img][/p][p]We tried a few things, but through this process I also learnt that I am very bad at UI design, so I settled on something that would use a minimalist approach to the UI, allowing the character and dice art (the visual stars of the show if you ask me) to really shine through. There is always room for improvement of course, but I think what we ended up with allowed new retro-arcade vibes to blossom through the game, much for the better.[/p][p][/p][p]Pfff, bad at UI design? Who would have ever guessed? I love seeing the evolution of games from early days to what they look like now, and this one is amazing. As cool as the tavern theme is, this retro arcade style just feels so unique and special.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Reminder: [/b]We're at MegaCon Manchester tomorrow! If you wanna come by for some chats or to get yourself one of these cool Dicealot sets, be sure to drop by! We'd love to meet you guys:)[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/fe599fc845d066418eb22337b6f1622a852e1a56.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][i]I've just noticed the dice in the picture and now it will forever irk me that it was so close to being an Albion's Road right there.[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/7e1df2be457565be83cf90bf72669177403b93df.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Behind the Dice: Farkle!
notes.notes: [h2]Another week, another Behind The Dice![/h2][p][/p][p]We hope you've all been enjoying the Dicealot demo so far! We've loved seeing all your feedback, screenshots and more in the [url="https://discord.com/invite/W4VzWHDF2U"]Discord[/url] so keep them coming! ([strike][i]also because I'd totally start a community spotlight section in the BTS with extra content duhh[/i][/strike])[/p][p][/p][h3]This week, our question for the devs was: [i]What were you inspirations for making Dicealot?[/i][/h3][p][/p][p]We love playing farkle in person, we have done it at group gatherings for years. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/e2521584fcc35e7ac26c2e735df092a3afb59840.jpg"][/img][/p][p]As game developers we had wanted to make a farkle roguelite (our favourite genre), for some time. We’re big fans of medieval European history, hence the setting. Originally it was going to be a much more slow paced, cozy game that told the story of King Harald and the Norman conquest of England. However, we realised we lacked the development power to deliver all of that and also a mechanically fun experience. So we focused on mechanical enjoyment, and sprinkled in our own medieval world around it.[/p][p][/p][p]And that's what's led to what you see today as Dicealot! [/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Megacon Live Manchester - We'll Be There![/h3][p][/p][p]Megacon is next weekend! If you're around, do come by! We have a booth set up there and you'll be able to meet Sirens (one of the devs) as well as Isaac and I (Carnotaur/Tvesha) from Yogscast Games - we also have some sweet goodies if you're around playing our game 👀[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/fe599fc845d066418eb22337b6f1622a852e1a56.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We've only got a limited amount of these so be there or be square (like a die. Although that's a cube. You know what I mean.) Come say hi![/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]See you in next week's BTS (and Megacon hopefully!)[/p]

notes.title: Behind the Dice: Enrage
notes.notes: [h2]Hello, and welcome back to Behind the Dice![/h2][p][/p][p]This week, we asked the devs: [i]What is something you have recently finished working on?[/i] They told us that they recently finished the [i]enrage[/i] system, where the foes get angrier the longer the fights last.[/p][p][/p][h3]Read on to find out more about what their thought process behind implementing the enrage system: [/h3][p][/p][p]The enrage system was a solution to the problem I created with re-rolls. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/7b60e4bd4e747fddd6b92dabdd5e7fb31b9f27d0.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Here's what the enrage symbol looks like in the game.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Re-rolls are necessary in the game, as they allow much more player agency within a ruleset (the ruleset of Farkle) that relies almost completely on RNG. Without rerolls the player would have even fewer ways to express their control. However, if we give the player too many re-rolls, they have too much control, and basically nullify the challenge of the game. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/577e24df6a7cffbcf32337b8cf5d77c588f18723.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/d95d1554eb69a9ac50c3d4012c01ad872d28376a.png"][/img][/p][p][i]As you can see, the enemy really doesn't like you re-rolling and is now enraged x2. Oops.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Currently there are ways to amass great amounts of re-rolls, but because that is a build choice, it comes at the expense of other things like multiplication and raw PWR. This would lead to a situation where players understandably chose builds that gave them the most control, but they actually ended up playing a very boring game, of lots and lots of tiny scoring hands. This is not what Dicealot is about. We want big numbers. [/p][p][/p][p]The worst thing about these builds is that whilst reliable, they make the game incredibly slow. So the enrage system is a simple mechanic that essentially makes the enemies hit you harder the longer the fight lasts, by rolling extra opponent dice. Because of this, these boring slow builds are no longer viable.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/d574471fe29333507c2bbf61094f2f4bbf8b6762.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/59a8a9537410d08322376acee20934bf04d02641.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]Look at those extra dice. That hurts.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Like everything else, its also another fun variable to play with. So we are adding some things that react to enemy rage, and including the rage timer as a variable when it comes to higher difficulties.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]If you want to know more about enrage, or have any other questions about the game and its development process, ask us here and we may just include it in our next Behind the Dice![/p]

notes.title: Behind the Dice: Burn Damage
notes.notes: [p]We've been chatting with the developers about Dicealot and asked them some questions we thought you'd find interesting. Welcome to our new series: [b]Behind the Dice[/b]! With each Behind the Dice, we'll be diving into different aspects of the game's development and design.[/p][p][/p][p]For our first Behind the Dice, we're exploring the burn damage mechanic. We asked the devs: [i]What's been going well recently? Tell us about something you made that you're really proud of, or something that came together easier than expected.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Here's what they had to say:[/p][p][/p][p]Since getting some early feedback about this, I had wanted to include a way for players to deal damage and win fights, which feels quite different from the ''regular'' way of building PWR and striking. There are only really a few inputs the player has, so having this new DMG source react to one of those was important, and tying it to ''on roll'' meant that a build utilising it would focus more on rolling than striking. [/p][p][/p][p]However, since striking is generally the only time a player gets hurt, it was important to try and balance it so striking would still be necessary, and you couldn't just ''roll your way to victory'' without ever running the risk of taking DMG in return. We also added some stuff like cleansing all burn stacks on Farkle, to keep this new method tied to the underlying rules of the game. [/p][p][/p][p]I settled on the idea of building up large numbers of ''Burn'' on the enemy, and having them take damage every time the player rolled, but also losing stacks when they take damage, to prevent the values getting out of hand or making it too strong. Also I chose [i]burn[/i] over [i]poison[/i] because it felt a little more thematically appropriate, and poison is a bit boring (albeit more recognisable for most players.).[/p][p][/p][p]Here's what the burn dice look like:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/363f6fa7ce732da549d47101951863ac590e43dc.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Funnily enough, while our producers were testing the burn damage, we uh... realized it may need some more tweaking[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/f507f7e46c00a0a0df210cd0bf9e9319020827f1.png"][/img][/p][p]Not a single strike was made and they have nearly wiped out the enemy which is pretty much what the devs [i]didn't[/i] want![/p]

notes.title: Dice Dimensions and What's New!
notes.notes:
Hear ye fellow dice-rollers!

I know it's been quiet on our end, but big things are brewing in the kingdom of Dicealot! We've been hard at work, and we're excited to share some updates that are sure to get your dice rolling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/f3bd2e1a3e5e79a1b3aff58ccc88198e4e4f032e.png[/img]

[h2]Dice Dimensions Event[/h2]

First up, we're thrilled to be part of the Dice Dimensions Steam event, running from March 5th to 12th! If you've been curious about Dicealot, now's the perfect time to check us out! Our demo is live so give it a try if you haven't yet!

[h2]What's New [/h2]

We've been working on some cool new additions to spice up your Dicealot adventures!

Act 3: We're introducing new Quests and Bosses that will be sure to test your skills!

New Map, New Shop: Say goodbye to the old single-shop setup - we're implementing a brand new map screen that lets you choose from multiple different shops between fights.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/77ac505ab1d5f171536b98de88bdc3a5a69c088b.png[/img]

We do heartily hope thou dost enjoy thy sojourn within our Kingdom, whether thou hast dwelt here since the dawning or art but newly come. Stayest thou tuned for tidings yet to come, and may fortune smile upon the bold!

notes.title: November for Dicealot!
notes.notes:
Hello fellow dice-rollers!

Here's a quick low down on what we've been up to last month!

[h2][b][url=https://gamayo.co.uk/2024/11/22/gamayo-success-at-wx/]GaMaYo![/url][/b][/h2]

Our first event with a playable build of Dicealot, we got to see first-hand playthroughs (as well as backseat game everyone that tried our demo) and got tons of great feedback.

Sir Dicealot was in attendance, teaching people the base game of Farkle and non-lethally dueling them on the arena of dice!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45057648/4d728fb358d9783c3308cf84842ce565d4c87d45.jpg[/img]

You can read an interview from the event with the dev team [url=https://gamayo.co.uk/2024/11/21/gamayo-23-showcase-26-dicealot-at-gamayo/]here[/url]

[h2][b]Admin![/b][/h2]

Everyone's favourite, we've been building up the backend so that we can get ourselves positioned for a successful release.

That means talking to publishers, putting various business development structures in place and all the other boring, paperwork related things required for us to support the game.

[h2][b]Development![/b][/h2]

Development in November was mostly focused on creating a more dynamic tutorial (give it a try if you haven't yet!) and making the game easier to play for new players. Of course there's always bug fixes going on, and more recently we've been implementing a post-battle reward screen (with individual opponents having their own weighted loot-tables).

Thanks for all the support so far and stay tuned for more news on a possible release date and updated features coming soon!

notes.title: Demo Update - V0.5.15
notes.notes:
Greetings fellow Questers!

Yesterday's update targeted a few big pieces of feedback from Nextfest as well as squashing the cause of a common crash

[b]New Features[/b]

- Auto-banking - Once you roll, double click on any dice to automatically send it to the bottom row and bank it. You can still drag if you prefer but this should speed up grinding through those hands in your 1s and 5s builds!

- Manual dice re-positioning on the board - Want to sort your dice on the board or remove those pesky overlaps? Click and drag the dice somewhere else on the game board.

[b]Bug fixes[/b]

- Implented a fix for the crashing when banking a 6 dice combo. This hit quite a few people so please let us know if you still hit this crash after this update!

Also included are various balance and price changes for existing quest and power dice

As always, jump on our discord if you want to chat with us, make suggestions, or report any issues!

[url=Dicealot Discord]https://discord.gg/XTB2XB4PSp[/url]
